# Next Action

`sales.obj.core.next_action` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> The single specific thing that must happen next, with an owner and a due date. Deliberately singular — that is the discriminator, and it is what separates this from a task list. A deal with six next actions has none, because nothing has been prioritised and every one of them can be deferred by pointing at another. The three clauses are each load-bearing: "specific" means a stranger could tell you whether it happened, "owner" means a named side and preferably a named person, "due date" means a date somebody agreed to rather than a date we invented. "Keep in touch", "circle back next quarter" and "await their feedback" fail all three and are the most common contents of the field in every CRM ever built.


Also called: `Next Step`, `Commitment`, `Action Item`, `Follow-up`

## Constraints

- **`na.one_open_per_deal`** Exactly one action may be open per deal at a time.
- **`na.needs_owner_and_date`** An action without an owner and a due date cannot enter stateopen.
- **`na.cannot_own_their_action`** We cannot mark an action owned by them as done. Onlyobservation of their behaviour discharges it.
- **`na.replacement_is_explicit`** Superseding an action must mark the prior one supersededin the same pass, or two live actions exist and therefore none does.
- **`na.no_chase_before_due`** Do not chase before due_at. Chasing early teaches the buyerthat our dates are not real. _(soft)_


## Business rules

- **`na.exactly_one_open_per_deal`** An open deal carries exactly one open next action. Six is zero — nothing has been prioritised, so every one of them can be deferred by pointing at another.
- **`na.open_deal_must_have_one`** An open deal with no next action must be flagged in the same pass, not at the next pipeline review. The absence is the finding; a review that discovers it a fortnight later has already lost the fortnight.
- **`na.must_be_owned_and_dated`** An action without both an owner and a due date is not a next action. Record it as undated rather than letting it count toward pipeline hygiene, because counting it is what makes the field worthless.
- **`na.unassigned_never_defaults_to_us`** An action with no stated owner is `unassigned`, never `us`. Silently adopting the buyer's commitments is how a rep ends up doing their internal selling and calling it follow-up.
- **`na.second_slip_escalates`** Rescheduling is the default response to an overdue action and it is usually wrong. A second slip on the same action means the action is not the blocker — escalate or change the action.
- **`na.activity_is_not_progress`** Actions with advances_stage = false must not count toward pipeline health. Otherwise the metric rewards logging follow-ups, which is the cheapest thing a rep can do and the least useful.

## Actions

- **Agree the next step before the call ends** (human) — Namedaction, named owner, named date, said out loud while both parties are still on the line. The single highest-return habit in sales and the one most consistently skipped in the last ninety seconds of a meeting.
- **Assign an explicit owner** (human) —
- **Put a date on an undated commitment** (human) —
- **Remind the owner** (agent) —
- **Chase the buyer's action** (human) — Chase the commitment, not the person. 'You mentioned Thursday for the questionnaire' outperforms 'just checking in' by a distance.
- **Escalate rather than reschedule** (human) — On a second slip.Rescheduling a twice-slipped action is how a deal spends a quarter looking active.
- **Replace the action with a better one** (human) — Frequently correct.An action nobody will do is worse than an action nobody agreed, because it stops the search for one that would move.
- **Cancel the action explicitly** (human) — A legitimate outcome.Cancelled and done are different facts and both beat an action that quietly rots.

## Metrics

- **deals_with_next_action** (percent) — Share of open deals carrying exactly oneopen, dated, owned action. The headline pipeline-hygiene number.
- **action_specificity_rate** (percent) — Share passing the stranger test. Unmeasurabletoday and the cheapest gap on the list to close.
- **on_time_completion_rate** (percent) — By owner side. Buyer-side completionis a far better predictor of the win than anything they say.
- **median_days_overdue** (days) —
- **second_slip_rate** (percent) — Actions slipping twice. Correlates with lossmore tightly than any single-slip measure.
- **action_to_stage_rate** (percent) — Completed actions that actually advanceda stage. Separates progress from activity.


## Examples

- **"Priya returns the security questionnaire by Thursday"** — Specific, owned by them,dated. A stranger could tell you whether it happened. This is the shape.
- **"Keep in touch"** — The classic misclassification — logged as a next step, countedin every hygiene metric, cannot slip because it was never due. It is the absence of a next action wearing one's clothes.
- **"Follow up next week"** — Owned by us, roughly dated, advances nothing. Passes mostCRM checks and moves no deal.
- **Six open tasks on one deal** — Reads as a well-managed opportunity in the activity log.Nothing is prioritised, so each one is deferrable by pointing at the others, and none is the next action.
- **Demo requested on Monday, no follow-up by Friday** — The buyer named the next actionfor free and the clock started when they said it. The highest-converting origin there is, missed in the most avoidable way.

> Eight of twelve patterns are executable, four blocked — the best-served object in the roster, because commitment.action and commitment.due_at are typed facts today. That makes the blocked four unusually pointed. The single highest-value gap is commitment.owner: the substrate emits what was committed and when, and never whose it is, so all eight executable patterns silently assume the action is ours — which is exactly the failure the object exists to prevent, and the mechanism by which a buyer's commitment becomes our chase. Close behind are commitment_completed (followup_sent only covers our own email actions, so na.overdue fires against commitments that were met) and derived.open_commitment_count, without which this object's defining rule — a deal with six next actions has none — cannot be enforced at all.
